title: Coral and the Protocol
premise: Ada Iversen smuggles stolen memories past orbital customs while tending a beacon whose origin no record explains. When the name 'Coral' appears on the manifest of the Meridian, a ship that never launched, Ada discovers the beacon is a countdown: two cryo-arks hold the remnants of humanity's diverging genetic lines, and the Protocol will wake only one. The manifest name belongs to a man whose memories Ada has been unknowingly carrying for years — fragments of the Protocol's designer, hidden inside contraband she herself smuggled. In the end, Ada must choose between erasing the man she has come to love and splitting the wake between both arks, sacrificing her own stored memories — and her knowledge of him — to do it.
about_author: D. M. Ravensworth is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing ship manifests before turning to fiction. They write from a coastal town where, they insist, the fog behaves suspiciously like static.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She runs a memory-chip shipment past orbital customs aboard a freighter, cool and practiced, then returns to maintain the nameless beacon in a decaying station ring. Emotional beat: competent solitude masking a low hum of unease about the beacon's missing origin records.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Never Was
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Cross-checking salvage manifests, she finds the Meridian — a ship with no launch record — carrying one passenger name: Coral. The beacon flickers in sync with her terminal. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery curdling into dread.

chapters.title: A Stranger in Her Own Cargo
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Among confiscated chips she finds a sealed memory core she has no record of taking, humming with the same frequency as the beacon. Emotional beat: the smuggler's confidence shaken by her own inventory.

chapters.title: Coral
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, waking with no context in a docking bay, drawn to Ada's beacon by instinct he can't explain. He confronts her. Emotional beat: mutual suspicion laced with an inexplicable, unwelcome familiarity.

chapters.title: Fragments Not Hers
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She plays a sliver of the sealed core and recognizes her own hands in memories she never lived — the designer's lab, the arks, a woman named Wren. Emotional beat: vertigo of inherited memory.

chapters.title: The Protocol
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, memories surfacing in dreams: he is a backup imprint of Dr. Elio Sarn, architect of the Protocol, which governs two cryo-arks and mandates a single-line wake. Emotional beat: horror at being someone's contingency plan.

chapters.title: Customs and Consequences
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. An inspector, Voss, flags her old shipments; the sealed core is now contraband of state interest. She hides Coral in her quarters. Emotional beat: loyalty forming under pressure.

chapters.title: Wren's Voice
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A memory fragment reveals Wren — Sarn's partner — argued to wake both arks, and was erased from the record. Coral realizes Ada resembles her. Emotional beat: grief for someone neither of them met.

chapters.title: The Beacon Speaks
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She decodes the beacon: it's a countdown and a dead-man switch, built by Sarn, keyed to his imprint — to Coral. Emotional beat: awe turning to responsibility.

chapters.title: What the Smuggler Kept
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Voss raids her locker; she burns her legit cargo to protect the core, becoming a fugitive in the only home she's known. Emotional beat: loss of the careful, compartmentalized life.

chapters.title: Running the Ring
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Ada and Coral evade customs drones through the station's underlevels, trading stories, growing close. Emotional beat: tenderness blooming in the cracks of crisis.

chapters.title: The First Ark
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. They reach the Meridian's true hull — the first ark, disguised as a derelict. Rows of sleepers from the diverged line. Emotional beat: reverence and the weight of ten thousand breaths held.

chapters.title: The Second Ark
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The beacon's signal leads to the second ark, hidden in the beacon itself — she has been living inside the other half of humanity's cradle. Emotional beat: her whole life reframed as stewardship.

chapters.title: Voss's Bargain
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The inspector corners them; she's a Protocol loyalist who believes one clean line must survive. She offers Ada amnesty for Coral's core. Emotional beat: temptation of safety against conviction.

chapters.title: The Designer's Confession
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A full memory sequence: Sarn built the dual-ark fail-safe with Wren, then, dying, split his imprint — half into the core, half into a man who would find it. Coral understands he was made to choose. Emotional beat: rage at being designed, then resolve.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The beacon hits final phase: the Protocol will auto-execute in seventy-two hours, waking one ark and venting the other. Emotional beat: clock-tight fear.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Sleeping
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. They plan to split the wake, but the Protocol requires an imprint to anchor both lines — and anchoring means the anchor's own memories are consumed as checksum. Emotional beat: the cost made explicit.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Coral volunteers, but Ada realizes the checksum will read the core — her contraband, her memories of him. One of them must be the anchor. Emotional beat: love stated plainly for the first time, as a goodbye.

chapters.title: Coral and the Protocol
chapters.summary: Climax. Coral's POV. He overrides the Protocol at the beacon's heart, splitting the wake, feeding his imprint into the checksum as Ada holds the connection open, weeping. Emotional beat: sacrifice as an act of authorship — he chooses who he is.

chapters.title: Two Dawns
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Both arks wake; sleepers emerge into the ring's restored light, including a woman with Wren's records and Coral's face but no memories of her. Emotional beat: bittersweet victory, grief braided with hope.

chapters.title: The Name on the Manifest
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She enters 'Coral' into the beacon's founding record, giving the ship that never flew its history, and begins recording new memories — deliberately, this time. Emotional beat: reclamation of memory as inheritance.

chapters.title: Beaconkeeper
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, epilogue. The stranger with Coral's imprint returns to the beacon, drawn by something he can't name; she offers her hand and her story. Emotional beat: quiet beginning — identity rebuilt not from what was lost, but what is chosen next.
